story: At 1:17 on a breezy, clear Tuesday afternoon, Gary, Donna, and Hal are gathered on Magnolia Loop, where Gary cheerfully heads off with Donna toward pickleball and leaves Hal in charge of the golf cart paperwork. Donna teases Hal about counting the cart lights and insists the extra ones are just the wind rearranging things, while Hal, gruffly pleased, reminds Gary to list both lights and speakers and keep the speakers quiet after ten. Meanwhile, over at Rosa's House, Rosa is determinedly working through her week's shifts to pick a dinner night that stays clear of Thursday mornings, ready to write it down in ink.
events: Rosa (rosa shift schedule): Look over this week's shifts and pick a dinner night that avoids Thursday morning, then write it in ink

gary.thought_process: Donna invited me to the rec center for pickleball and I never answered her. Hal is right here and I asked him to look over my Architectural Review form last tick. He's busy counting flamingos with Donna, so I shouldn't ask him again. Best move is to answer Donna, tell her I'm in for the court, and settle the form question with Hal so nobody feels dropped. I'll keep it short and friendly, with a plan for the form after the game.

parameters.content: You're on, Donna, I'll walk over with you. Hal, hold onto that form for me, and we'll go over the cart lights after the game.

donna.thought_process: Hal is counting my flamingos and asked how many are in the flock. I need to answer him directly rather than dodge. L-02 says three ornaments visible from the street, and I'd rather not hand him a violation on a silver platter, so I'll own it with charm and a little spin. Gary is still standing here too, and I've already invited him to the court, so once Hal has his answer I'll steer Gary toward the rec center. For this tick, answer Hal first.

parameters.content: Hal, honey, count them yourself, I trust you to be fair. It's three, and anything past that is just the wind rearranging them. Now don't you go filing paperwork before I've had my pickleball.

hal.thought_process: Gary asked me to look over his form before he files, and that's exactly the sort of by-the-book behavior I like to see. Cart mods need Architectural Review approval under L-01, so I'll encourage him to file it properly. Donna is dragging him off to pickleball, so I'll keep it short: tell him to bring the form by the board or the rec center and I'll check it. And a quiet word on Donna's flamingos can wait until I've got my count straight.

parameters.content: Glad to see you filing it right, Gary. Go play your pickleball, then bring the form to me after and I'll check it line by line. Lights and speakers both need to be listed, and keep the speakers off after ten.

rosa.thought_process: I've got the menu, grocery list, and chair count out on the dining table, and Thursday 8 AM is already inked in for Hal. The last step from my previous tick is penciling in a dinner night that avoids Thursday morning. Nobody's around to talk to, so I'll use the shift schedule to check my per-diem shifts and settle on an evening that works for all three neighbors. Then I can go invite them properly.

parameters.content: Look over this week's shifts and pick a dinner night that avoids Thursday morning, then write it in ink

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
